decisions.reason: As a newly launched and publicly announced security feature that fits the firm's secure-identity ecosystem, management is likely to continue backing it rather than admit the launch was premature.
Because an identity-linked payment wallet supports the firm's stated super-app and ecosystem strategy, the firm is likely to persist with it despite any early uncertainty.

This authenticator appears less central and less visibly committed than the platform products, but as a recent launch in the firm's security domain it would still more likely be retained for another year than withdrawn.
A payment and wallet framework with its own page suggests meaningful investment and commitment, which under escalation of commitment makes withdrawal unlikely so soon after launch.
Since this product was presented as a flagship and as part of the firm's future direction, management is highly likely to keep it to justify the strategic commitment and sunk investment.

An application shielding library builds directly on the firm's long-standing security capabilities and was given dedicated market visibility, so management would be inclined to continue it rather than write it off quickly.
